close_reason: Fixed in commit fa47ae8. Added prominent module-level rustdoc 'Single-user limitation' section disclosing that find_uniqueness_conflict is account-wide (not per-caller), that isPrivate visibility scoping is unimplemented, and explicitly naming what a multi-user backend MUST do (read principal_id, scope find_uniqueness_conflict by it when is_private is true, filter reads, reject cross-user mutations). Added an inline rustdoc note on find_uniqueness_conflict cross-referencing the module section so a reader of that function in isolation finds the caveat. Skipped optional (b) wiring principal_id through (no behaviour change for the single-user demo path) and optional (c) #[ignore] demo test (rustdoc with explicit MUST-language discharges the contributor-onboarding concern). All 32 tests pass; cargo doc with -D warnings clean.
description:
memory.rs:318-334 — find_uniqueness_conflict scans the account's Metadata store WITHOUT consulting caller identity. The UniquenessKey at memory.rs:182-188 includes is_private as a discriminator (shared/private don't conflict with each other — correct), but the per-user scoping for private metadata is unimplemented.

draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01 §3.1 wording:

  For private metadata (isPrivate: true), the server MUST enforce per-
  user uniqueness: each user may have at most one private Metadata
  object for each combination of relatedType, relatedId, and @type.
  The server internally may store multiple private Metadata objects for
  the same related-type combination (one per user), but each user can
  only see and modify their own.

So per spec: two different users can each have their OWN private Annotation on (Email, EM1, Annotation). The MemoryBackend currently rejects the second user's create with alreadyExists because the uniqueness scan is account-wide.

Combined with JMAP-ayoz.1 and JMAP-ayoz.2 (the unknown-accountId family) this is a single-user-only impl masquerading as a reference. The crate-level AGENTS.md explicitly says "isPrivate visibility scoping... Multi-user production deployments MUST override the default impl" — but the MemoryBackend's rustdoc does not flag this caveat.

Two issues bundled here:
1. The behavior is unsound for multi-user (silent wrong-answer alreadyExists).
2. The rustdoc on MemoryBackend at memory.rs:26-42 lists Metadata-specific behaviors and is silent about per-user-scoping. Contributors copying this impl into a multi-user backend will inherit the bug.

Fix: 
a) Add prominent rustdoc on MemoryBackend disclosing the single-user limitation under §3.1: "Per-user uniqueness scope is NOT implemented; this backend treats all callers as a single user. A multi-user backend MUST scope find_uniqueness_conflict by JmapBackend::principal_id(caller)."
b) Optionally wire principal_id() through find_uniqueness_conflict in the reference impl. Since CallerCtx = (), principal_id returns None, the existing account-wide scan remains the documented behavior, but the code path is wired and explicit.
c) Add a doc test or a #[ignore] marker test that explicitly shows the limitation so a contributor cargo-grepping for "principal_id" finds the hook.
title: MemoryBackend uniqueness scope is account-wide, not per-caller — silently wrong for multi-user private metadata
